sentences.zh: 衛青，字明德，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Wei Qing, styled Mingde, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qing, whose style was Mingde, came from Huating in Songjiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以薊州百戶降成祖，積功至都指揮僉事，蒞中都留守司事，改山東備倭。

translations.literal: As a company commander of Jizhou he surrendered to the Founding Emperor, and through accumulated merit rose to Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Capital Garrison, took charge of affairs at the Central Capital Garrison Command, and was reassigned to coastal defense against Japanese pirates in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He had surrendered to the Yongle Emperor as a hundred-household officer at Jizhou; through repeated service he rose to vice commander-in-chief of the capital garrison, directed affairs at the Central Capital garrison headquarters, and was then transferred to Shandong to guard against wokou raids.

sentences.zh: 永樂十八年二月，浦臺妖婦林三妻唐賽兒作亂。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighteenth year of Yongle, the demonic woman Tang Sai'er, wife of Lin San of Putai, raised rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yongle 18 (1420), Tang Sai'er of Putai—the wife of Lin San, a woman regarded as a sorceress—rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 自言得石函中寶書神劍，役鬼神，剪紙作人馬相戰鬥。

translations.literal: She claimed to have obtained from a stone casket a precious book and divine sword, to command ghosts and spirits, and to cut paper into men and horses that fought one another.
translations.idiomatic: She claimed a sacred book and magic sword from a stone chest, power over spirits, and the art of cutting paper figures that marched and fought like real armies.

sentences.zh: 徒眾數千，據益都卸石柵寨。

translations.literal: Her followers numbered several thousand; she seized the stockade at Xieshi in Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand adherents rallied to her, and she held the stockade at Xieshi in Yidu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 指揮高鳳敗歿，勢遂熾。

translations.literal: Commander Gao Feng was defeated and killed, and her power swiftly grew.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander Gao Feng was defeated and killed, her movement grew far stronger.

sentences.zh: 其黨董彥昇等攻下莒、即墨，圍安丘。

translations.literal: Her partisans Dong Yansheng and others captured Ju and Jimo and besieged Anqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Her lieutenants Dong Yansheng and others took Ju and Jimo and laid siege to Anqiu.

sentences.zh: 總兵官安遠侯柳升帥都指揮劉忠圍賽兒寨。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief, Marquis Anyuan Liu Sheng, led Regional Commander Liu Zhong to besiege Sai'er's stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The commander-in-chief, Marquis Anyuan Liu Sheng, led Regional Commander Liu Zhong in a siege of Sai'er's stronghold.

sentences.zh: 賽兒夜劫官軍。

translations.literal: Sai'er raided the government army by night.
translations.idiomatic: Sai'er struck the government camp in a night attack.

sentences.zh: 軍亂，忠戰死，賽兒遁去。

translations.literal: The army fell into disorder; Zhong died in battle and Sai'er escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The army broke apart; Zhong was killed in the fighting and Sai'er slipped away.

sentences.zh: 比明，升始覺，追不及，獲賊黨劉俊等及男女百余人。

translations.literal: By dawn Sheng only then realized what had happened; he could not overtake her, but captured the rebel Liu Jun and more than a hundred men and women.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Sheng at last learned what had happened. He failed to catch Sai'er but seized the rebel Liu Jun and more than a hundred captives, men and women.

sentences.zh: 而賊攻安丘益急，知縣張、丞馬撝死戰，賊不能下，合莒、即墨眾萬余人以攻。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the rebels pressed Anqiu ever harder; Magistrate Zhang and Assistant Magistrate Ma Huo fought to the death, yet the rebels could not take it, and they combined the forces of Ju and Jimo—more than ten thousand men—to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the rebels redoubled their assault on Anqiu. Magistrate Zhang and Assistant Magistrate Ma Huo fought to the death, and though the city still held, the rebels massed more than ten thousand men from Ju and Jimo for a combined attack.

sentences.zh: 青方屯海上，聞之，帥千騎晝夜馳至城下。

translations.literal: Qing was then encamped on the coast; hearing of this, he led a thousand horsemen and galloped day and night to the foot of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was stationed on the coast at the time. When word reached him, he led a thousand cavalry and rode day and night to the city.

sentences.zh: 再戰，大敗之，城中亦鼓噪出，殺賊二千，生擒四千余，悉斬之。

translations.literal: After a second battle he routed them utterly; the city also sallied forth with clamor, killing two thousand rebels, capturing alive more than four thousand, and beheading them all.
translations.idiomatic: In a second engagement he routed them completely. The garrison sallied out with a great clamor, killing two thousand rebels, taking more than four thousand alive, and executing every captive.

sentences.zh: 時城中旦夕不能支，青救稍遲，城必陷。

translations.literal: At that time the city could scarcely hold another day or night; had Qing's relief come slightly later, the city would certainly have fallen.
translations.idiomatic: The city was on the verge of collapse; had Qing arrived even a little later, Anqiu would surely have been lost.

sentences.zh: 比賊敗，升始至，青迎謁。

translations.literal: When the rebels had already been defeated, Sheng at last arrived; Qing went out to meet and pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the rebels were beaten did Sheng arrive. Qing went out to greet him.

sentences.zh: 升怒其不待己，捽之出。

translations.literal: Sheng, angry that Qing had not waited for him, seized him and threw him out.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, furious that Qing had acted without waiting for him, seized him and had him dragged away.

sentences.zh: 是日，鰲山衛指揮王真亦以兵百五十人殲賊諸城，賊遂平。

translations.literal: That same day Wang Zhen, commander of Aoshan Guard, also with a hundred and fifty men annihilated rebels at Zhucheng, and the rebellion was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Wang Zhen, commander of Aoshan Guard, destroyed rebel forces at Zhucheng with a hundred and fifty men, and the uprising was fully suppressed.

sentences.zh: 而賽兒卒不獲。

translations.literal: Yet Sai'er was never captured in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Sai'er herself was never captured.

sentences.zh: 帝賜書勞青，切責升。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a letter commending Qing and sharply rebuking Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Qing a letter of commendation and rebuked Sheng in the sternest terms.

sentences.zh: 尚書吳中等劾升，且言升冒青功。

translations.literal: Minister Wu Zhong and others impeached Sheng, also saying that Sheng had usurped Qing's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wu Zhong and others impeached Sheng, charging that he had claimed Qing's achievements as his own.

sentences.zh: 於是下升獄，而擢青山東都指揮使，真都指揮同知，、撝左右參議，賞賚有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sheng was cast into prison, while Qing was promoted to regional commander of Shandong, Zhen to vice regional commander, and Huo to Left and Right Participating Secretariat Councillor, with rewards apportioned by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was imprisoned. Qing was promoted to regional commander of Shandong; Zhen was made vice regional commander; Ma Huo was made Left and Right Participating Secretariat Councillor; and rewards were distributed according to merit.

sentences.zh: 青還備倭海上。

translations.literal: Qing returned to coastal defense against Japanese pirates on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Qing returned to coastal defense against the wokou.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事系獄。

translations.literal: Before long he was imprisoned on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was imprisoned on a charge of misconduct.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，帝念其功，釋之，俾復職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande the Emperor, recalling his merit, released him and restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 1 (1426), remembering his service, the Emperor released him and restored him to his post.

sentences.zh: 時京師營繕役繁，調及防海士卒。

translations.literal: At that time construction labor in the capital was heavy, and coastal-defense troops were being conscripted for it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time construction work in the capital was heavy, and coastal-defense troops were being drafted for it.

sentences.zh: 青以為言，得番代。

translations.literal: Qing spoke on the matter and obtained rotation of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Qing appealed on their behalf and secured a system of rotating tours of duty.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，進都督僉事，尋卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, he was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong came to the throne, he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief, and soon afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 青有孝行，善撫士卒，居海上十余年，海濱人思之，請於朝，立祠以祀。

translations.literal: Qing had filial conduct and was skilled at comforting troops; he dwelt on the sea more than ten years, and the people of the coast missed him, petitioning the court to erect a shrine in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was known for filial devotion and for winning the loyalty of his soldiers. After more than ten years on the coast, the coastal people missed him so deeply that they petitioned the court to build a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 傳子至孫錞。

translations.literal: The line passed to his son and on to his grandson Chun.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed through his son to his grandson Chun.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖時，督神機營，屢加太保兼太子太師。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he directed the Divine Engine Corps and was repeatedly advanced to Grand Guardian and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing era he commanded the Divine Engine Corps and was repeatedly promoted to grand guardian and grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 四傳至時泰。

translations.literal: After four generations the line reached Shitai.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations later the line reached Shitai.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，掌後府。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign he held charge of the Rear Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen era he headed the Rear Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，懷鐵券，闔門十七人皆赴井死。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, clasping the iron certificate of privilege, the whole household of seventeen persons all threw themselves into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, he clutched the family's iron certificate of privilege, and all seventeen members of his household threw themselves into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 董興，長垣人。

translations.literal: Dong Xing was a native of Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xing came from Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 初為燕山右衛指揮使，累遷署都指揮同知。

translations.literal: At first he was commander of the Right Guard of Yan Mountains, and through successive promotions became acting Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He began as commander of the Right Guard of Yan Mountains and rose through successive posts to acting vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 正統中，新建伯李玉等舉興將才，進署都指揮使，京營管操。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong reign the newly created Earl Li Yu and others recommended Xing's talent as a general; he was advanced to acting Regional Commander and put in charge of drill in the Capital Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign the newly created Earl Li Yu and others praised his generalship. He was promoted to acting regional commander and placed in charge of drill in the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 復用薦，擢署都督僉事，充右參將，從寧陽侯陳懋討鄧茂七，破余黨於建寧，進都督同知。

translations.literal: Again on recommendation he was promoted to acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief, served as Right Assistant Regional Commander, followed Marquis Ningyang Chen Mao in campaigning against Deng Maoqi, broke the remnant faction at Jianning, and was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended again, he was made acting vice commissioner-in-chief and right assistant regional commander. He followed Marquis Ningyang Chen Mao against Deng Maoqi, crushed the rebel remnant at Jianning, and was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 南海賊黃蕭養圍廣州，安鄉伯張安、都指揮王清戰死，賊眾攻城益急。

translations.literal: The South Sea rebel Huang Xiaoyang besieged Guangzhou; Earl Anxiang Zhang An and Regional Commander Wang Qing died in battle, and the rebel host pressed the assault ever harder.
translations.idiomatic: The South Sea rebel Huang Xiaoyang besieged Guangzhou. Earl Anxiang Zhang An and Regional Commander Wang Qing were killed in battle, and the rebels pressed the assault ever harder.

sentences.zh: 詔拜興左副總兵，調江西、兩廣軍往討，而以侍郎孟鑒贊理軍務。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xing Left Assistant Commander-in-Chief, mobilized armies of Jiangxi and the Two Guangs to campaign, and made Vice Minister Meng Jian coordinator of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Xing left assistant commander-in-chief, mobilized troops from Jiangxi and the Two Guangs, and made Vice Minister Meng Jian coordinator of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 興用天文生馬軾自隨。

translations.literal: Xing took with him the astronomical clerk Ma Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Xing took along the astronomical clerk Ma Shi as his adviser.

sentences.zh: 興果銳，不能戢下，軾戒之。

translations.literal: Xing was indeed bold and sharp but could not restrain his subordinates; Shi admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was bold and aggressive but could not discipline his men; Shi warned him against it.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年二月，師至廣州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Jingtai the army reached Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Jingtai 1 (1450) the army reached Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊舟千余艘，勢甚熾，而征兵未至，諸將請濟師。

translations.literal: The rebels had more than a thousand boats and their power was very strong, yet the levies had not arrived; the generals asked for reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had more than a thousand boats and their strength was formidable, but reinforcements had not yet arrived. The generals asked for more troops.

sentences.zh: 軾曰：「廣民延頸久矣，即以狼兵往擊，猶拉朽耳。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "The people of Guang have long craned their necks in hope; even if we send only the Lang troops to strike, it will be like pulling rotten wood apart."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "The people of Guangdong have waited long enough. Even if we send only the Lang militia against them, it will be like tearing rotten timber apart.

sentences.zh: 興從之。

translations.literal: Xing followed this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Xing followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 既而兵大集，進至大洲擊賊，殺溺死者萬余人，余多就撫。

translations.literal: Before long the armies massed in full; advancing to Dazhou they struck the rebels, and more than ten thousand were killed or drowned; the remainder largely submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the full force assembled. Advancing to Dazhou, they attacked the rebels. More than ten thousand were killed or drowned, and most of the remainder surrendered.

sentences.zh: 蕭養中流矢死，函首以獻，俘其父及子等，余黨皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Xiaoyang was struck by an arrow and died; his head was boxed and presented; his father and sons were captured; the remaining partisans were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyang was struck by an arrow and killed. His head was sent to the capital in a box; his father and sons were captured; and the remaining rebels were executed.

sentences.zh: 論功，進右都督，留鎮廣東。

translations.literal: In reckoning merit he was advanced to Right Commissioner-in-Chief and left to garrison Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief and left to garrison Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 給事中黃士俊劾興寬縱，降其官。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Huang Shijun impeached Xing for leniency and indulgence, and his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Huang Shijun impeached Xing for excessive leniency, and his rank was reduced.

sentences.zh: 明年復職。

translations.literal: The next year he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 久之，召還，分督京營。

translations.literal: After a long while he was recalled and given divided command of the Capital Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled to share command of the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 與曹吉祥結姻，冒「奪門」功，封海寧伯。

translations.literal: He formed a marriage alliance with Cao Jixiang, usurped merit from the "Gate Seizure," and was enfeoffed as Earl of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: He allied himself by marriage with Cao Jixiang, claimed credit for the Gate Seizure coup, and was enfeoffed as Earl of Haining.

sentences.zh: 未幾，充總兵官，鎮遼東，予世券。

translations.literal: Before long he was made commander-in-chief, garrisoned Liaodong, and granted a hereditary certificate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made commander-in-chief, posted to Liaodong, and granted a hereditary certificate of privilege.

sentences.zh: 議革「奪門」者爵，興以守邊得免。

translations.literal: When there was discussion of stripping titles from those of the "Gate Seizure," Xing was spared because he was guarding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated stripping titles from those who had profited from the Gate Seizure, Xing was spared because he was guarding the frontier.

sentences.zh: 吉祥誅，乃奪興爵，仍右都督，發廣西立功。

translations.literal: When Jixiang was executed, Xing's title was then stripped; he remained Right Commissioner-in-Chief and was sent to Guangxi to earn merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: After Jixiang was executed, Xing's noble title was revoked. He remained right commissioner-in-chief and was sent to Guangxi to win merit in the field.

sentences.zh: 以錦衣李貴薦，復爵，總兵宣府，再予世券。

translations.literal: On recommendation of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard Li Gui, his title was restored; he was made commander-in-chief at Xuanfu and again granted a hereditary certificate.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Li Gui of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, his title was restored. He was made commander-in-chief at Xuanfu and again granted a hereditary certificate.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嗣位，罷還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong succeeded, he was dismissed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong succeeded to the throne, Xing was dismissed and recalled.

sentences.zh: 已，停世襲。

translations.literal: Thereafter hereditary succession was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary succession of his title was then suspended.

sentences.zh: 家居十余年卒。

translations.literal: He dwelt at home more than ten years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for more than ten years and then died.

sentences.zh: 德陽人趙鐸反，自稱趙王，漢州諸賊皆歸之。

translations.literal: Zhao Duo of Deyang rebelled, styled himself King of Zhao, and the bandits of Han prefecture all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Duo of Deyang rose in rebellion, proclaimed himself King of Zhao, and the bandits of Hanzhou all rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 連番眾，數陷城，殺將吏。

translations.literal: In successive waves his host grew; they repeatedly took cities and killed commanders and officials.
translations.idiomatic: His forces swelled in wave after wave; they repeatedly captured towns and killed commanders and officials.

sentences.zh: 遣其黨何文讓及僧悟升掠安嶽諸縣。

translations.literal: He sent his partisans He Wenrang and the monk Wusheng to plunder the counties of Anyue and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his lieutenants He Wenrang and the monk Wusheng to raid Anyue and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 洪斬悟升，生擒文讓。

translations.literal: Hong beheaded Wusheng and captured Wenrang alive.
translations.idiomatic: Hong killed Wusheng and took Wenrang alive.

sentences.zh: 鐸將逼成都，官軍分三路討。

translations.literal: Duo was about to press on Chengdu; the government army divided into three routes to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: As Duo advanced toward Chengdu, government forces moved against him in three columns.

sentences.zh: 洪偕都指揮寧用趨彰明，賊引去。

translations.literal: Hong together with Regional Commander Ning Yong hastened toward Zhangming, and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hong advanced toward Zhangming with Regional Commander Ning Yong, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 追至梓潼朱家河，力戰，賊少卻。

translations.literal: Pursuing to the Zhu family river at Zitong, they fought fiercely and the rebels fell back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing them to the Zhu Family River at Zitong, they fought fiercely and the rebels gave ground.

sentences.zh: 洪乘勝陷陣，後軍不繼，為賊所圍，左右跳蕩，殺賊甚眾，力竭而死。

translations.literal: Hong, pressing the victory, plunged into the enemy line; the rear army did not follow, and he was surrounded by rebels; he leaped about on every side, killing very many rebels, and died when his strength was spent.
translations.idiomatic: Hong pressed the advantage and charged into the enemy ranks, but the rear units failed to follow. Surrounded, he fought on every side and killed many rebels before his strength gave out and he fell.

sentences.zh: 洪勇敢，善撫士，號令嚴，蜀將無及之者。

translations.literal: Hong was brave, skilled at comforting soldiers, and strict in command; among Shu generals none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was brave, won the loyalty of his men, and enforced strict discipline. Among the generals of Shu, none could match him.

sentences.zh: 既死，官軍奪氣。

translations.literal: After he died, the government army lost its spirit.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the government army lost heart.

sentences.zh: 而四川都指揮僉事臨淮劉雄亦戰死。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Liu Xiong of Linhuai, Vice Regional Commander of Sichuan, also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiong of Linhuai, vice regional commander of Sichuan, also fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 雄剛勁，遇敵輒前，嘗捕賊漢州，生擒七十余人。

translations.literal: Xiong was firm and forceful; whenever he met the enemy he pressed forward; he had once captured bandits at Han prefecture and taken more than seventy alive.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was hard and unyielding and always led from the front. He had once crushed bandits at Hanzhou and taken more than seventy alive.

sentences.zh: 及鐸亂，追之羅江大水河，手馘數人，賊連敗。

translations.literal: When Duo's rebellion broke out, he pursued him to the Great Water River at Luojiang, personally beheading several men, and the rebels suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo's rebellion broke out, he pursued him to the Great Water River at Luojiang, killed several rebels with his own hand, and drove the enemy into repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 千戶周鼎傷，雄前救之，徑奔賊陣，叢刺死。

translations.literal: Thousand-Household Zhou Ding was wounded; Xiong went forward to rescue him, charged straight into the rebel line, and was killed by a volley of spears.
translations.idiomatic: When Thousand-Household Zhou Ding was wounded, Xiong rushed forward to save him, charged straight into the rebel ranks, and was killed by a hail of spears.

sentences.zh: 詔贈洪都督同知，予祭葬，子節襲都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted Hong the rank of Vice Commissioner-in-Chief, bestowed sacrificial burial, and his son Jie inherited the post of Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was posthumously made vice commissioner-in-chief, granted state funeral honors, and his son Jie inherited the post of vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 雄贈都指揮同知，賜祭，命子襲職，超二官。

translations.literal: Xiong was posthumously granted Vice Regional Commander, given sacrificial honors, and his son was ordered to inherit the post with advancement of two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was posthumously made vice regional commander, granted sacrificial honors, and his son was ordered to inherit his post with a promotion of two ranks.

sentences.zh: 洪雖死，綿竹典史蕭讓帥鄉兵擊鐸，破之。

translations.literal: Though Hong had died, the Mianzhu district clerk Xiao Rang led local militia against Duo and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Hong was dead, Xiao Rang, district clerk of Mianzhu, led local militia against Duo and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 官兵頻進擊，其黨稍散去。

translations.literal: The government army pressed attacks repeatedly, and his partisans gradually dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces pressed the attack again and again, and Duo's followers gradually scattered.

sentences.zh: 鐸勢孤，帥余賊趨彰明。

translations.literal: Duo's power was isolated; he led the remaining rebels toward Zhangming.
translations.idiomatic: Isolated and weakened, Duo led the remnant of his force toward Zhangming.

sentences.zh: 千戶田儀等設伏梓潼，而參將周貴直搗其巢。

translations.literal: Thousand-Household Tian Yi and others set an ambush at Zitong, while Assistant Regional Commander Zhou Gui struck straight at their nest.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-Household Tian Yi and others laid an ambush at Zitong while Assistant Regional Commander Zhou Gui attacked Duo's base directly.

sentences.zh: 賊大敗，夜奔石子嶺。

translations.literal: The rebels were utterly defeated and fled by night to Shizi Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were routed and fled by night toward Shizi Ridge.

sentences.zh: 儀亟進，斬鐸，賊盡平。

translations.literal: Yi pressed forward swiftly, beheaded Duo, and the rebels were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yi pressed forward at once, killed Duo, and the rebellion was fully suppressed.

sentences.zh: 成化元年五月也。

translations.literal: This was in the fifth month of the first year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: This took place in the fifth month of Chenghua 1.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝將以谷登為甘肅副總兵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Emperor was about to appoint Gu Deng assistant commander-in-chief of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Emperor was about to appoint Gu Deng assistant commander-in-chief in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 李賢言登不任，玉老成。

translations.literal: Li Xian said Deng was not equal to the task and Yu was seasoned and steady.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian argued that Deng was unfit for the post and that Yu was seasoned and reliable.

sentences.zh: 乃復以為都督僉事、右副總兵，鎮守涼州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yu was again made Vice Commissioner-in-Chief and Right Assistant Commander-in-Chief, garrisoning Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was therefore reappointed vice commissioner-in-chief and right assistant commander-in-chief to garrison Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 咎咂族叛，會兵平之，進都督同知。

translations.literal: The Jiuza tribe rebelled; he gathered troops and pacified them, and was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiuza tribe rebelled, he assembled troops and suppressed them, and was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 成化四年，滿俊亂固原，白圭舉玉為總兵官，統左右參將夏正、劉清討之，兵分為七。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chenghua Man Jun rebelled at Guyuan; Bai Gui recommended Yu as commander-in-chief, directing the Left and Right Assistant Regional Commanders Xia Zheng and Liu Qing against him, with the army divided into seven.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 4, Man Jun rebelled at Guyuan. Bai Gui recommended Yu as commander-in-chief, with Assistant Regional Commanders Xia Zheng and Liu Qing under him. The army was divided into seven columns.

sentences.zh: 玉與總督項忠抵石城，賊已數敗。

translations.literal: Yu and Grand Coordinator Xiang Zhong reached Shicheng; the rebels had already suffered several defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Grand Coordinator Xiang Zhong reached Shicheng after the rebels had already suffered several defeats.

sentences.zh: 會毛忠死，玉亦被圍，中流矢，力戰得出。

translations.literal: When Mao Zhong died, Yu was also surrounded, was struck by an arrow, and fought his way out by main force.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao Zhong fell, Yu too was surrounded, took an arrow wound, and fought his way out.

sentences.zh: 相持兩月，大小百十戰，竟平之。

translations.literal: They faced one another two months; in large and small engagements numbering more than a hundred and ten, the rebellion was at last pacified.
translations.idiomatic: After two months of stalemate and more than a hundred engagements large and small, the rebellion was finally suppressed.

sentences.zh: 進左都督，掌右府事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Left Commissioner-in-Chief and put in charge of affairs of the Right Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left commissioner-in-chief and placed in charge of the Right Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 自訴前西堡功，命增俸百石，掌耀武營。

translations.literal: Pleading his earlier merit at Xibao, he was ordered an increase of a hundred piculs of salary and put in charge of the Yaowu Corps.
translations.idiomatic: On his own petition citing his earlier victory at Xibao, he was granted an additional hundred piculs of salary and command of the Yaowu Corps.

sentences.zh: 六年充左副總兵，從朱永出延綏。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as Left Assistant Commander-in-Chief and followed Zhu Yong out to Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as left assistant commander-in-chief and campaigned in Yan-sui under Zhu Yong.

sentences.zh: 五月，河套部入犯，玉帥眾禦卻之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Ordos tribes invaded; Yu led the host and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Ordos tribes invaded; Yu led his troops and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒。

translations.literal: The year after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 贈固原伯，謚毅敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Earl of Guyuan, with the posthumous name Yimin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Guyuan with the posthumous name Yimin.

sentences.zh: 玉雖起仆隸，勇決過人，善撫士，所至未嘗衄。

translations.literal: Though Yu rose from menial servitude, his courage and decisiveness surpassed others; he was skilled at comforting soldiers, and wherever he went he never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yu had risen from servile origins, his courage and decisiveness were exceptional, he won the loyalty of his men, and he never met defeat wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 滿俊之叛，據石城險，屢敗官軍，玉戰最力。

translations.literal: In Man Jun's rebellion, holding the perilous position at Shicheng, he repeatedly defeated the government army; Yu fought with the greatest exertion.
translations.idiomatic: In Man Jun's rebellion, the rebels held the strong position at Shicheng and repeatedly defeated government forces; Yu fought harder than any other commander.

sentences.zh: 及論功，只賜秩一級，時惜其薄。

translations.literal: When merit was reckoned, he was granted only one step in rank; at the time people regretted how meager it was.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were distributed, he received only a single rank promotion, which many at the time thought far too little.

sentences.zh: 子文，襲指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Wen inherited the post of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wen inherited the post of regional commander.

sentences.zh: 仇鉞，字廷威，鎮原人。

translations.literal: Chou Yue, styled Tingwei, was a native of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chou Yue, whose style was Tingwei, came from Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 初以傭卒給事寧夏總兵府，大見信愛。

translations.literal: At first as a hired soldier he served in the Ningxia commander-in-chief's office and was greatly trusted and favored.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a hired soldier in the Ningxia commander-in-chief's headquarters and won deep trust.

sentences.zh: 會都指揮僉事仇理卒，無嗣，遂令鉞襲其世職，為寧夏前衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: When Vice Regional Commander Chou Li died without heir, Yue was ordered to inherit his hereditary post as Vice Regional Commander of the Forward Guard of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Regional Commander Chou Li died without an heir, Yue was ordered to inherit his hereditary post as vice regional commander of the Forward Guard of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 理，江都人，故鉞自稱江都仇氏。

translations.literal: Li was a native of Jiangdu; therefore Yue styled himself of the Chou clan of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Li was from Jiangdu, so Yue styled himself a member of the Chou clan of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 再以破賊功，進都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Again on merit in defeating rebels he was advanced to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: For further merit in defeating rebels he was promoted to vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 正德二年用總制楊一清薦，擢寧夏遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde, on recommendation of Grand Coordinator Yang Yiqing, he was promoted to Mobile Corps General of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 2, on Yang Yiqing's recommendation, he was made mobile corps general of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 五年，安化王寘鐇及都指揮何錦、周昂，指揮丁廣反。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Prince of Anhua Zhu Zhifan together with Regional Commanders He Jin and Zhou Ang and Commander Ding Guang rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Prince of Anhua, Zhu Zhifan, rebelled together with Regional Commanders He Jin and Zhou Ang and Commander Ding Guang.

sentences.zh: 鉞時駐城外玉泉營，聞變欲遁去。

translations.literal: Yue was then encamped outside the city at Yuquan Camp; hearing of the uprising he wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was camped outside the city at Yuquan Camp. When he heard of the revolt, his first impulse was to flee.

sentences.zh: 顧念妻子在城中，恐為所屠滅，遂引兵入城。

translations.literal: But considering that his wife and children were in the city and fearing they would be slaughtered, he led his troops into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering that his wife and children were still in the city and fearing they would be massacred, he led his troops inside.

sentences.zh: 解甲覲寘鐇，歸臥家稱病，以所將兵分隸賊營。

translations.literal: He doffed his armor to pay court to Zhifan, returned home and lay abed claiming illness, and distributed the troops he commanded among the rebel camps.
translations.idiomatic: He laid aside his armor to pay homage to Zhifan, went home and feigned illness, and distributed his troops among the rebel camps.

sentences.zh: 錦等信之，時時就問計。

translations.literal: Jin and the others trusted him and came repeatedly to ask his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and the others trusted him and came to him again and again for advice.

sentences.zh: 鉞亦謬輸心腹。

translations.literal: Yue also falsely confided his inner thoughts to them.
translations.idiomatic: Yue in turn pretended to confide in them fully.

sentences.zh: 而陰結壯士，遣人潛出城，令還報官軍旦夕至。

translations.literal: Meanwhile he secretly rallied stout fellows, sent men stealthily out of the city, and had them return to report that the government army would arrive at any moment.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he rallied loyal fighters and sent men out of the city to spread word that government troops would arrive at any moment.

sentences.zh: 鉞因紿錦、廣，宜急出兵守渡口，遏東岸兵，勿使渡河。

translations.literal: Yue therefore deceived Jin and Guang, saying they ought urgently to send troops to guard the crossing and block the army on the east bank from crossing the river.
translations.idiomatic: He then deceived Jin and Guang, urging them to rush troops to the river crossing to block government forces on the east bank from crossing.

sentences.zh: 錦、廣果傾營出，而昂獨守城。

translations.literal: Jin and Guang indeed emptied the camps and went out, while Ang alone remained to guard the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Guang emptied the camps and marched out, leaving Ang alone to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 寘鐇以祃牙召鉞，鉞稱病亟。

translations.literal: Zhifan summoned Yue with a military tally; Yue claimed his illness was severe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifan summoned Yue with a military tally, but Yue pleaded that his illness was severe.

sentences.zh: 昂來視，鉞方堅臥呻吟。

translations.literal: Ang came to visit him; Yue was then lying rigidly abed and groaning.
translations.idiomatic: When Ang came to visit, Yue lay rigidly in bed, groaning.

sentences.zh: 伏卒猝起，捶殺昂。

translations.literal: Hidden soldiers suddenly rose up and beat Ang to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden soldiers leaped up and beat Ang to death.

sentences.zh: 鉞乃被甲橫刀，提其首，躍馬大呼，壯士皆集，徑馳詣寘鐇第，縛之。

translations.literal: Yue then donned armor, sword across his body, seized Ang's head, leaped on his horse and shouted loudly; the stout fellows all gathered, galloped straight to Zhifan's residence, and bound him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then donned his armor, sword in hand, seized Ang's head, mounted his horse with a great shout, and rallied his men. They galloped straight to Zhifan's residence and seized him.

sentences.zh: 傳寘鐇令，召錦等還，而密諭其部曲以擒寘鐇狀。

translations.literal: Transmitting Zhifan's order, he summoned Jin and the others back, while secretly instructing his troops on the fact that Zhifan had been captured.
translations.idiomatic: Issuing orders in Zhifan's name, he recalled Jin and the others, while secretly telling his troops that Zhifan had been captured.

sentences.zh: 眾遂大潰。

translations.literal: The host thereupon broke apart in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel forces collapsed in disorder.

sentences.zh: 錦、廣單騎走賀蘭山，為邏卒所獲，舉事凡十八日而敗。

translations.literal: Jin and Guang fled alone on horseback to Helan Mountain and were captured by frontier soldiers; the whole affair lasted only eighteen days before failure.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Guang fled alone toward Helan Mountain and were captured by frontier troops. The entire rebellion collapsed within eighteen days.

sentences.zh: 先是，中朝聞變，議以神英為總兵官，而命鉞為副。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the central court heard of the uprising, it was debated to make Shen Ying commander-in-chief and appoint Yue as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the central court learned of the revolt, it was proposed to make Shen Ying commander-in-chief with Yue as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 俄傳鉞降賊，欲追敕還。

translations.literal: Before long word spread that Yue had surrendered to the rebels, and the court wished to recall the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word spread that Yue had joined the rebels, and the court considered recalling his appointment.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊廷和曰：「鉞必不從賊，令知朝廷擢用，誌當益堅。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe said: "Yue will certainly not follow the rebels; let him know the court has promoted him, and his resolve will only grow firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe said, "Yue will never join the rebels. If he learns the court has promoted him, his resolve will only grow firmer.

sentences.zh: 不然，棄良將資敵人耳。」

translations.literal: Otherwise we abandon a good general and supply the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise we abandon a fine general and strengthen the enemy.

sentences.zh: 乃不追。

translations.literal: The recall was not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: The recall was not issued.

sentences.zh: 事果定。

translations.literal: The affair was indeed settled.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 而劉瑾匿陜西總兵官曹雄，盡以鉞功歸之，鉞竟無殊擢。

translations.literal: But Liu Jin concealed Shaanxi commander-in-chief Cao Xiong and attributed all Yue's merit to him; Yue in the end received no special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: But Liu Jin shielded Shaanxi commander-in-chief Cao Xiong and credited him with all of Yue's achievements. Yue received no special promotion.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史閻睿訟其功，詔奪俸三月。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Yan Rui pleaded his merit, and an edict stripped three months' salary.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Yan Rui pleaded Yue's case, but an edict stripped him of three months' salary instead.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，始進署都督僉事，充寧夏總兵官。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Yue was at last advanced to acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief and made commander-in-chief of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, Yue was at last promoted to acting vice commissioner-in-chief and made commander-in-chief of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 尋論功，封鹹寧伯，歲祿千石，予世券。

translations.literal: Before long, in reckoning merit, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Xianning with a yearly stipend of a thousand piculs and granted a hereditary certificate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for his merit, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Xianning with an annual stipend of a thousand piculs and granted a hereditary certificate of privilege.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，召掌三千營。

translations.literal: The next winter he was summoned to command the Three Thousand Corps.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he was recalled to command the Three Thousand Corps.

sentences.zh: 七年二月拜平賊將軍，偕都御史彭澤討河南盜劉惠、趙鐩，以中官陸訚監其軍。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year he was appointed Pacification General and, together with Censor-in-Chief Peng Ze, campaigned against the Henan bandits Liu Hui and Zhao San, with the eunuch Lu Yan supervising the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year he was appointed Pacification General. Together with Censor-in-Chief Peng Ze he campaigned against the Henan bandits Liu Hui and Zhao San, with the eunuch Lu Yan supervising the army.

sentences.zh: 未至，而參將馮禎戰死洛南，賊勢益熾。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Assistant Regional Commander Feng Zhen died in battle at Luonan and the rebels grew stronger still.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, Assistant Regional Commander Feng Zhen was killed at Luonan and rebel strength surged.

sentences.zh: 已，聞官軍將至，遂奔汝州。

translations.literal: Before long, hearing that the government army was coming, they fled to Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that government troops were approaching, they fled to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 又聞官軍扼要害，乃走寶豐，復由舞陽、遂平轉掠汝州東南，敗奔固始，抵潁州，屯朱臯鎮。

translations.literal: Hearing again that the government army held the strategic points, they fled to Baofeng, then by Wuyang and Suiping turned to plunder southeast of Ruzhou; defeated, they fled to Gushi, reached Yingzhou, and encamped at Zhugao town.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that government forces held the key passes, they fled to Baofeng, then swept through Wuyang and Suiping into southeastern Ruzhou. Beaten again, they fled to Gushi, reached Yingzhou, and encamped at Zhugao.

sentences.zh: 永順宣慰彭明輔等擊之，賊倉猝渡河，溺死者二千人。

translations.literal: Peng Mingfu of Yongshun Pacification Commission and others struck them; the rebels crossed the river in haste and two thousand drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Mingfu of the Yongshun Pacification Commission and others attacked them. The rebels crossed the river in panic and two thousand drowned.

sentences.zh: 余眾走光山，鉞追及之。

translations.literal: The remainder fled to Guangshan; Yue overtook them.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fled to Guangshan, and Yue caught up with them.

sentences.zh: 命諸將神周、姚信、時源、金輔左右夾擊，賊大敗，斬首千四百有奇。

translations.literal: He ordered the generals Shen Zhou, Yao Xin, Shi Yuan, and Jin Fu to attack from both flanks; the rebels were utterly defeated and more than fourteen hundred heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Shen Zhou, Yao Xin, Shi Yuan, and Jin Fu to attack from both flanks. The rebels were routed and more than fourteen hundred heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 湖廣軍亦破其別部賈勉兒於羅田。

translations.literal: The Huguang army also defeated their separate band under Jia Mianer at Luotian.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang forces also defeated their splinter band under Jia Mianer at Luotian.

sentences.zh: 賊沿途潰散。

translations.literal: The rebels broke up and scattered along the route.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke up and scattered along the roads.

sentences.zh: 自六安陷舒城，復還光山，至商城。

translations.literal: From Lu'an they took Shucheng, returned to Guangshan, and reached Shangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: They took Shucheng from Lu'an, returned to Guangshan, and reached Shangcheng.

sentences.zh: 官軍追之急，賊復南攻六安。

translations.literal: The government army pressed them hard; the rebels again attacked Lu'an from the south.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed by government troops, the rebels turned south to attack Lu'an again.

sentences.zh: 將陷，時源等涉河進，敗之七里岡。

translations.literal: As the city was about to fall, Shi Yuan and others crossed the river and advanced, defeating them at Qiligang.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall, Shi Yuan and others crossed the river, advanced, and defeated them at Qiligang.

sentences.zh: 賊趨廬州，至定遠西又敗。

translations.literal: The rebels moved toward Luzhou and were defeated again west of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels moved toward Luzhou and were beaten again west of Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 還至六安，分其眾為二。

translations.literal: Returning to Lu'an, they divided their force in two.
translations.idiomatic: They returned to Lu'an and split their force in two.

sentences.zh: 劉惠與趙鐩二弟鐇、鎬帥萬余人，北走商城。

translations.literal: Liu Hui with Zhao San's two younger brothers Zhao Fan and Zhao Hao led more than ten thousand men north toward Shangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui and Zhao San's younger brothers Zhao Fan and Zhao Hao led more than ten thousand men north toward Shangcheng.

sentences.zh: 而鐩道遇其徒張通及楊虎遺黨數千人，勢復振，掠鳳陽，陷泗、宿、睢寧、定遠。

translations.literal: San on the road met his follower Zhang Tong and several thousand remnants of Yang Hu's faction; their power revived again, and they plundered Fengyang and took Si, Su, Suining, and Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the road San met his follower Zhang Tong and several thousand remnants of Yang Hu's band. Their strength revived, and they raided Fengyang and captured Si, Su, Suining, and Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 於是澤與鉞計，使神周追鐩，時源、金輔追惠，姚信追勉兒。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ze and Yue planned to send Shen Zhou after San, Shi Yuan and Jin Fu after Hui, and Yao Xin after Mianer.
translations.idiomatic: Ze and Yue then divided their forces: Shen Zhou pursued San, Shi Yuan and Jin Fu pursued Hui, and Yao Xin pursued Mianer.

sentences.zh: 勉兒、鐩復合，周信連敗之宿州，追奔至應山，其眾略盡。

translations.literal: Mianer and San joined again; Zhou and Xin repeatedly defeated them at Suzhou and pursued them in flight to Yingshan until their host was nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: Mianer and San joined forces again. Zhou and Xin defeated them repeatedly at Suzhou and pursued them to Yingshan until their band was nearly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 鐩發懷度牒，潛至江夏。

translations.literal: San produced a monk's ordination certificate from his bosom and slipped secretly to Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: San produced a monk's ordination certificate and slipped secretly into Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 飯村店，軍士趙成執送京師，伏誅。

translations.literal: At Fancun inn, the soldier Zhao Cheng seized him and sent him to the capital, where he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At an inn in Fancun village, the soldier Zhao Cheng seized him and sent him to the capital, where he was executed.

sentences.zh: 源、輔追劉惠，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Yuan and Fu pursued Liu Hui and won victory in battle after battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Fu pursued Liu Hui and won a series of victories.

sentences.zh: 惠窘走南召，指揮王謹追及於土地嶺，射中惠左目，自縊死。

translations.literal: Hui, hard pressed, fled south to Nanzhao; Commander Wang Jin overtook him at Tudi Ridge, shot him in the left eye, and he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Hui fled south to Nanzhao. Commander Wang Jin overtook him at Tudi Ridge, shot him in the left eye, and he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 勉兒數為都指揮朱忠、夏廣所敗，獲之項城丁村。

translations.literal: Mianer had been repeatedly defeated by Regional Commanders Zhu Zhong and Xia Guang and was captured at Ding village in Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mianer had been repeatedly defeated by Regional Commanders Zhu Zhong and Xia Guang and was captured at Ding village in Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 余黨邢本道、劉資及楊寡婦等先後皆被擒。

translations.literal: The remaining partisans Xing Bendao, Liu Zi, the Widow Yang, and others were all captured in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining leaders such as Xing Bendao, Liu Zi, and the Widow Yang were captured one after another.

sentences.zh: 凡出師四月，而河南賊悉平。

translations.literal: In all, within four months of taking the field, the Henan rebels were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within four months of taking the field, the Henan rebels were entirely suppressed.

sentences.zh: 趙鐩，一名風子，文安諸生也。

translations.literal: Zhao San, also called Fengzi, was a licentiate of Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao San, also known as Fengzi, was a licentiate scholar of Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 劉七等亂起，鐩挈家匿渚中，賊驅之登陸，將汙其妻女。

translations.literal: When the disorders of Liu Qi and others broke out, San took his family to hide in the islets; the bandits drove them ashore and were about to violate his wife and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: When the disorders led by Liu Qi and others broke out, San hid his family among the river islets. Bandits drove them ashore and were about to violate his wife and daughters.

sentences.zh: 鐩素驍健，有膂力，手格殺二賊。

translations.literal: San had always been bold and strong, with great physical power, and killed two bandits with his bare hands.
translations.idiomatic: San had always been bold and powerful and killed two bandits with his bare hands.

sentences.zh: 賊聚執之，遂入其黨為之魁。

translations.literal: The bandits gathered and seized him, and he thereupon entered their faction as its leader.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits seized him, and he soon became their leader.

sentences.zh: 賊專事淫掠，鐩稍有智計，定為部伍，勸其黨無妄殺。

translations.literal: The bandits devoted themselves chiefly to rape and plunder; San had some resourcefulness, organized them into units, and urged his followers not to kill recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits devoted themselves chiefly to rape and plunder. San had some shrewdness, organized them into units, and urged his followers not to kill without cause.

sentences.zh: 移檄府縣，約官吏師儒毋走避，迎者安堵。

translations.literal: He sent proclamations to prefectures and counties, stipulating that officials and teachers need not flee but would be secure if they welcomed him.
translations.idiomatic: He issued proclamations to prefectures and counties promising that officials and teachers who did not flee would be left unmolested.

sentences.zh: 由是橫行中原，勢出劉六等上。

translations.literal: Thus he ranged across the central plain, his power surpassing that of Liu Liu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he ranged across the central plain with power surpassing that of Liu Liu and the others.

sentences.zh: 嘗攻鈞州五日，以馬文升方家居，舍之去。

translations.literal: He once attacked Jun prefecture for five days; because Ma Wensheng was then living in retirement at home, he spared it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He once besieged Jun prefecture for five days, but spared it and withdrew because Ma Wensheng was living in retirement there.

sentences.zh: 有司遣人賫招撫榜至，鐩具疏附奏言：「今群奸在朝，舞弄神器，濁亂海內，誅戮諫臣，屏棄元老，舉動若此，未有不亡國者。

translations.literal: When the authorities sent men bearing placards of amnesty, San submitted a memorial attached to his reply, saying: "Now wicked men hold court, wielding the imperial regalia, befouling the realm, executing remonstrating ministers, and casting aside elder statesmen. Conduct such as this has never failed to bring a state to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When officials sent amnesty placards, San submitted a memorial saying, "Wicked men now hold court, wield the imperial regalia, befoul the realm, execute remonstrating ministers, and cast aside elder statesmen. A state that acts thus cannot fail to perish.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下睿謀獨斷，梟群奸之首以謝天下，即梟臣之首以謝群奸。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty, with sagacious resolve acting alone, to behead the leaders of the wicked faction to appease the realm, and then behead this minister's head to appease the wicked faction.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to act with decisive wisdom, behead the leaders of the wicked faction to appease the realm, and then behead this minister's head to appease them.

sentences.zh: 其桀黠如此。

translations.literal: Such was his audacious cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his audacious cunning.

sentences.zh: 鉞既平河南賊，移師會陸完，共滅劉七等於江北。

translations.literal: After Yue had pacified the Henan rebels, he moved his army to join Lu Wan and together destroyed Liu Qi and the others north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the Henan rebels, Yue moved his army to join Lu Wan and together destroyed Liu Qi and the others north of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 論功，進世侯，增祿百石，仍督三千營。

translations.literal: In reckoning merit he was advanced to Hereditary Marquis, given an increase of a hundred piculs of stipend, and still directed the Three Thousand Corps.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to hereditary marquis, granted an additional hundred piculs of stipend, and retained command of the Three Thousand Corps.

sentences.zh: 八年，大同有警，命充總兵官，統京軍禦之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when Datong was alarmed, he was ordered to serve as commander-in-chief and lead the capital army to defend against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when Datong was threatened, he was made commander-in-chief and led capital troops to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 鉞上五事，中請遣還京操邊軍，停京軍出征，以省公私之擾，尤切時弊。

translations.literal: Yue submitted five proposals, among them asking to send back capital-drilled frontier troops, halt capital-army expeditions, and spare public and private disruption—especially cutting at the abuses of the day.
translations.idiomatic: Yue submitted five proposals, including sending back capital-drilled frontier troops and halting capital-army expeditions to spare public and private disruption—proposals that struck directly at the abuses of the day.

sentences.zh: 時不能用。

translations.literal: At the time they could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they were not adopted.

sentences.zh: 鉞既至，值寇犯萬全沙河。

translations.literal: When Yue had arrived, the raiders were invading the Sha River at Wanquan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue arrived, raiders were attacking the Sha River region at Wanquan.

sentences.zh: 擊之，斬首三級，而軍士亡者二十余人，寇亦引去。

translations.literal: He struck them, took three heads, yet more than twenty soldiers were lost, and the raiders also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked them, took three heads, lost more than twenty soldiers, and the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 奏捷蒙賚，朝論恥之。

translations.literal: He reported victory and received rewards, but court opinion regarded it with shame.
translations.idiomatic: He reported victory and received rewards, but court opinion regarded the affair as shameful.

sentences.zh: 帝詔諸邊將入侍豹房。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered frontier generals to attend him in the Leopard Quarter.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered frontier generals to attend him in the Leopard Quarter.

sentences.zh: 鉞嘗一入，後輒力辭。

translations.literal: Yue went in once, but afterward firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yue attended once, but thereafter firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，稱疾解營務。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year he claimed illness and resigned camp duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the tenth year he claimed illness and resigned his camp duties.

sentences.zh: 詔給軍三十人役其家。

translations.literal: An edict granted thirty soldiers to serve his household.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted thirty soldiers to serve his household.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，再起督三千營，掌前府事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, Yue was again appointed to direct the Three Thousand Corps and hold charge of the Forward Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, Yue was again appointed to command the Three Thousand Corps and head the Forward Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 未上卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: Before he could take office he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take office he died at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 謚武襄。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous name Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 子昌以病廢，孫鸞嗣侯。

translations.literal: His son Chang was disqualified by illness; his grandson Luan inherited the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang was disqualified by illness; his grandson Luan inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，怙寵通邊，磔死，爵除。

translations.literal: In the Shizong reign, relying on favor he traded across the frontier and was dismembered and executed; the title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shizong reign he abused imperial favor to trade across the frontier, was executed by dismemberment, and the title was abolished.

sentences.zh: 神英，字景賢，壽州人。

translations.literal: Shen Ying, styled Jingxian, was a native of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ying, whose style was Jingxian, came from Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 天順初，襲父職，為延安衛指揮使，守備寧塞營，屢將騎兵，從都督張欽等征討有功。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he inherited his father's post as regional commander of Yan'an Guard, garrisoned Ningsai Camp, repeatedly led cavalry, and followed Regional Commander Zhang Qin and others on campaigns with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign he inherited his father's post as commander of Yan'an Guard, garrisoned Ningsai Camp, repeatedly led cavalry in campaigns under Regional Commander Zhang Qin and others, and won merit.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，尚書王復行邊，薦英有謀勇，進都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua, Minister Wang Fu toured the frontier and recommended Ying for strategy and courage; he was advanced to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 1, Minister Wang Fu toured the frontier and recommended Ying for strategy and courage. He was promoted to vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 以從征滿四功，遷都指揮使，充延綏右參將。

translations.literal: On merit in the campaign against Man Si he was transferred to Regional Commander and served as Right Assistant Regional Commander of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in the campaign against Man Si he was made regional commander and right assistant regional commander of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 屢敗乚加思蘭兵，進署都督僉事。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated the forces of Yibolisi Khan and was advanced to acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly defeated the forces of Yibolisi Khan and was promoted to acting vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 巡撫余子俊築邊墻，命英董役，工成受賚。

translations.literal: When Grand Coordinator Yu Zijun built the frontier wall, Ying was ordered to supervise the labor; when the work was completed he received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Coordinator Yu Zijun built the frontier wall, Ying supervised the work and received rewards when it was completed.

sentences.zh: 久之，充總兵官，鎮守寧夏，移延綏，復移宣府。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made commander-in-chief, garrisoned Ningxia, moved to Yan-sui, and again moved to Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made commander-in-chief, garrisoned Ningxia, then Yan-sui, and then Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 弘治改元，移大同。

translations.literal: When Hongzhi began a new reign he was moved to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongzhi reign began he was transferred to Datong.

sentences.zh: 十一年，馬市開，英違禁貿易，寇掠蔚州又不救，言官連劾，召還閑住。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the horse market opened, Ying traded in violation of the prohibition; when raiders plundered Yuzhou he did not rescue, and censors impeached him in succession; he was recalled to idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the horse market opened, Ying traded in violation of the ban. When raiders plundered Yuzhou he failed to rescue, censors impeached him repeatedly, and he was recalled to idle residence.

sentences.zh: 尋起督果勇營。

translations.literal: Before long he was reappointed to direct the Brave Fruit Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reappointed to command the Brave Fruit Corps.

sentences.zh: 嘗充右參將，從朱暉禦寇延綏。

translations.literal: He had once served as Right Assistant Regional Commander and followed Zhu Hui in defending Yan-sui against raiders.
translations.idiomatic: He had once served as right assistant regional commander under Zhu Hui in defending Yan-sui against raiders.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，寇犯宣府，與李俊並充左參將，帥京軍以援。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong succeeded, raiders invaded Xuanfu; he and Li Jun were both made Left Assistant Regional Commanders and led capital troops to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong succeeded, raiders invaded Xuanfu. He and Li Jun were both made left assistant regional commanders and led capital troops to reinforce the frontier.

sentences.zh: 尋以都督同知僉事左府，剿近畿劇賊，進右都督。

translations.literal: Before long, as Vice Commissioner-in-Chief he took part in affairs of the Left Military Commission, suppressed fierce bandits near the capital, and was advanced to Right Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served as vice commissioner-in-chief in the Left Military Commission, suppressed fierce bandits near the capital, and was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 正德五年，給事中段豸劾英老，命致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengde, Supervising Secretary Duan Zhi impeached Ying as old and he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 5, Supervising Secretary Duan Zhi impeached Ying as too old, and he was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 當是時，劉瑾竊政。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Jin usurped government power.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Jin usurped government power.

sentences.zh: 總兵官曹雄等以附瑾得重權。

translations.literal: Commanders-in-chief such as Cao Xiong gained heavy authority by attaching themselves to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders-in-chief such as Cao Xiong gained heavy authority by attaching themselves to Jin.

sentences.zh: 英素習瑾，厚賄之。

translations.literal: Ying had long been familiar with Jin and bribed him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had long been familiar with Jin and bribed him heavily.

sentences.zh: 因自陳邊功，乞敘錄，特詔予伯爵。

translations.literal: He thereupon pleaded his frontier merit and begged for recognition; a special edict granted him the rank of earl.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded his frontier merit and begged for recognition; a special edict granted him the rank of earl.

sentences.zh: 吏、兵二部持之，下廷議。

translations.literal: The Ministries of Personnel and War held back, and the matter was sent down for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministries of Personnel and War held back, and the matter was sent to court for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 而廷臣希謹指，無不言當封者，遂封涇陽伯，祿八百石。

translations.literal: But court ministers followed the cautious line; none said he should not be enfeoffed, and he was therefore enfeoffed as Earl of Jingyang with a stipend of eight hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers followed the cautious line; none opposed enfeoffment, and he was made Earl of Jingyang with a stipend of eight hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，寘鐇反，命充總兵官討之。

translations.literal: Before long, when Zhifan rebelled, he was ordered to serve as commander-in-chief to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when Zhifan rebelled, he was ordered to serve as commander-in-chief against him.

sentences.zh: 未至，賊已滅。

translations.literal: Before he arrived the rebels had already been destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived the rebels had already been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 其秋，瑾敗，為言官所劾。

translations.literal: That autumn, when Jin fell, he was impeached by censors.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, after Jin fell, censors impeached him.

sentences.zh: 詔奪爵，以右都督致仕。

translations.literal: An edict stripped his title and he retired as Right Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped his title and he retired as right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 越二年卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 子周，輸粟為指揮僉事。

translations.literal: His son Zhou gained the post of Vice Regional Commander by presenting grain.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou gained the post of vice regional commander by presenting grain.

sentences.zh: 累官都指揮使，充延綏右參將。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he rose to Regional Commander and served as Right Assistant Regional Commander of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive offices he rose to regional commander and served as right assistant regional commander of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 正德六年命以所部兵討河南流賊，數有功，再進都督同知。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde he was ordered to campaign against Henan roaming bandits with the troops under his command; he won merit repeatedly and was twice advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 6 he was ordered to campaign against Henan roaming bandits with his troops, won repeated merit, and was twice promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 賊平，遂以副總兵鎮山西。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified he was made Assistant Commander-in-Chief to garrison Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were pacified he was made assistant commander-in-chief to garrison Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，寇大入寧武關，躪忻、定襄、寧化。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year the raiders entered in force through Ningwu Pass and overran Xin, Dingxiang, and Ninghua.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the ninth year raiders entered in force through Ningwu Pass and overran Xin, Dingxiang, and Ninghua.

sentences.zh: 周擁兵不戰，軍民死者數千。

translations.literal: Zhou held his troops without fighting; several thousand soldiers and civilians died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou held his troops without fighting, and several thousand soldiers and civilians died.

sentences.zh: 詔巡撫官執歸京師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the grand coordinator to seize him and return him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the grand coordinator to seize him and return him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 周潛結貴近，行至易州，偽稱病，自陳戰功。

translations.literal: Zhou secretly cultivated connections with powerful favorites; reaching Yizhou he falsely claimed illness and pleaded his battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou secretly cultivated connections with powerful favorites. Reaching Yizhou, he falsely claimed illness and pleaded his battle merit.

sentences.zh: 帝乃宥周罪，盡削其秩，為總旗，而輸粟指揮如故。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon pardoned Zhou's crime, stripped all his ranks, and made him Chief Company Officer, while his grain-presented commandership remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pardoned Zhou's crime, stripped all his ranks, and made him chief company officer, while his grain-presented commandership remained.

sentences.zh: 已，夤緣江彬入豹房，驟復都督，賜國姓，典兵禁中。

translations.literal: Before long, through connections with Jiang Bin he entered the Leopard Quarter, was suddenly restored to regional commander, granted the imperial surname, and put in charge of troops within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, through connections with Jiang Bin he entered the Leopard Quarter, was suddenly restored to regional commander, granted the imperial surname, and put in charge of palace troops.

sentences.zh: 遂與彬相倚為聲勢，納賄不貲。

translations.literal: He then relied on Bin for mutual power and accepted bribes beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He then relied on Bin for mutual power and accepted bribes beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 彬敗，周亦下獄，伏誅。

translations.literal: When Bin fell, Zhou was also cast into prison and executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin fell, Zhou was cast into prison and executed.

sentences.zh: 正德四年，雄上言：「故事，布、按二司及兵備道臣文移達總兵官者，率由都司轉達。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde, Xiong submitted a memorial, saying: "By precedent, documents from the provincial administration commission and surveillance commission and from the military defense circuit reach the commander-in-chief only after transmission through the regional military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 4, Xiong submitted a memorial saying, "By precedent, documents from the provincial administration and surveillance commissions and from the military defense circuit reach the commander-in-chief only through the regional military commission.

sentences.zh: 今邊務亟，征調不時，都司遠在會城，往返千里，恐誤軍機。

translations.literal: Now frontier affairs are urgent and levies are not timely; the regional commission is far away at the provincial seat, a round trip of a thousand li, and I fear military opportunity may be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Now frontier affairs are urgent and levies are not timely. The regional commission is far away at the provincial seat, a round trip of a thousand li, and I fear military opportunity may be lost.

sentences.zh: 乞如巡撫大同例，徑呈總兵官便。」

translations.literal: I beg that, following the precedent for the Datong grand coordinator, documents be presented directly to the commander-in-chief for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that, following the precedent for the Datong grand coordinator, documents be presented directly to the commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書曹元希瑾意，覆如其言。

translations.literal: Minister of War Cao Yuan, courting Jin's wishes, approved as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Cao Yuan, courting Jin's wishes, approved as he said.

sentences.zh: 既復受瑾屬，奏雄鎮守未佩印，宜如各邊例，特賜印以重其權。

translations.literal: Having again received a commission from Jin, he memorialized that Xiong, garrisoning but not yet wearing his seal, ought, like other frontiers, to be granted a special seal to weight his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Having again received a commission from Jin, he memorialized that Xiong, though garrisoning the frontier, had not yet received his seal and ought, like other frontiers, to be granted a special seal to weight his authority.

sentences.zh: 乃進雄署都督同知，以延綏總兵官吳江所佩征西將軍印佩之，而別鑄靖虜將軍印予江。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiong was advanced to acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief; he was given the Western Campaign General's seal worn by Yan-sui commander-in-chief Wu Jiang, while a separate Pacify the Barbarians General seal was cast for Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was advanced to acting vice commissioner-in-chief and given the Western Campaign General's seal worn by Yan-sui commander Wu Jiang, while a separate Pacify the Barbarians General seal was cast for Jiang.

sentences.zh: 及總督才寬禦寇沙窩為所殺，雄擁兵不救。

translations.literal: When Grand Coordinator Cai Kuan was killed by raiders at Shawa, Xiong held his troops and did not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Coordinator Cai Kuan was killed by raiders at Shawa, Xiong held his troops and did not rescue.

sentences.zh: 佯引罪，乞解兵柄，令子謐賫奏詣京師。

translations.literal: Feigning repentance, he begged to be relieved of military authority and had his son Mi carry a memorial to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Feigning repentance, he begged to be relieved of military authority and had his son Mi carry a memorial to the capital.

sentences.zh: 瑾異謐貌，妻以從女，而優詔褒雄，令居職如故，糾者反被責。

translations.literal: Jin was struck by Mi's appearance, gave him a collateral daughter in marriage, and issued a gracious edict praising Xiong, ordering him to remain in office as before; those who impeached him were instead rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was struck by Mi's appearance, gave him a collateral daughter in marriage, and issued a gracious edict praising Xiong and ordering him to remain in office; those who impeached him were rebuked instead.

sentences.zh: 寘鐇反寧夏，雄聞變，即統兵壓境上。

translations.literal: When Zhifan rebelled in Ningxia, Xiong heard of the uprising and at once massed troops along the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhifan rebelled in Ningxia, Xiong heard of the uprising and at once massed troops along the border.

sentences.zh: 令都指揮黃正以兵三千入靈州，固士卒心，約鄰境刻期討。

translations.literal: He ordered Regional Commander Huang Zheng to enter Lingzhou with three thousand men to steady the soldiers' hearts and arranged with neighboring territories a fixed date for the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Regional Commander Huang Zheng to enter Lingzhou with three thousand men to steady morale and arranged with neighboring territories a fixed date for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 密焚大、小二壩積草，與守備史鏞等奪河西船，盡泊東岸。

translations.literal: He secretly burned the stored grass at the Great and Small Dams and, with Garrison Commander Shi Yong and others, seized boats on the west bank of the river and moored them all on the east bank.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly burned the stored grass at the Great and Small Dams and, with Garrison Commander Shi Yong and others, seized boats on the west bank and moored them all on the east bank.

sentences.zh: 賊黨何錦懼，急帥兵出守大壩，以防決河。

translations.literal: The rebel He Jin, in fear, urgently led troops out to guard the Great Dam lest the river be breached.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel He Jin, in fear, urgently led troops out to guard the Great Dam lest the river be breached.

sentences.zh: 雄乃令鏞潛通書仇鉞，俾從中舉事，賊遂成擒。

translations.literal: Xiong then had Yong secretly send a letter to Chou Yue, enabling him to act from within; the rebels were thus captured.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong then had Yong secretly send a letter to Chou Yue, enabling him to act from within, and the rebels were captured.

sentences.zh: 是役也，功雖成於鉞，而居外布置，賊不內顧，雄有勞焉。

translations.literal: In this campaign, though the achievement was realized by Yue, Xiong had merit in deploying outside so that the rebels could not look inward.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign, though the achievement belonged to Yue, Xiong had merit in deploying outside so the rebels could not look inward.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，瑾以平賊功歸之，進左都督。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, Jin attributed the merit of pacifying the rebels to him and advanced him to Left Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, Jin attributed the merit of pacifying the rebels to him and advanced him to left commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 謐亦官千戶。

translations.literal: Mi was also given the rank of Thousand-Household.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was also given the rank of thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 雄不安，引咎自劾，推功諸將，降旨慰勞。

translations.literal: Xiong was uneasy, pleaded guilt and impeached himself, and pushed merit onto the other generals; an edict comforted and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was uneasy, pleaded guilt and impeached himself, and credited the other generals; an edict comforted and praised him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，瑾敗，言官交劾。

translations.literal: Before long Jin fell and censors impeached him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jin fell and censors impeached him in succession.

sentences.zh: 降指揮僉事，尋征下獄，以黨逆論死，籍其家。

translations.literal: He was reduced to Vice Regional Commander, then summoned and cast into prison, condemned to death as a partisan of rebellion, and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: He was reduced to vice regional commander, then summoned, imprisoned, condemned to death as a partisan of rebellion, and his household goods were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 詔宥之，與家屬永戍海南，遇赦不原。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned him; he and his family were permanently exiled to Hainan, without remission even on general amnesties.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned him; he and his family were permanently exiled to Hainan, without remission even on general amnesties.

sentences.zh: 雄長子謙，讀書能文，有機略，好施予。

translations.literal: Xiong's eldest son Qian could read and write, had resourcefulness, and delighted in giving.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's eldest son Qian was literate, resourceful, and generous.

sentences.zh: 故參政李侖、主事孔琦家貧甚，雄請周恤其妻子，以勸廉吏，謙意也。

translations.literal: Former Participating Secretariat Councillor Li Lun and Director Kong Qi were extremely poor; Xiong asked that their wives and children be supported to encourage honest officials—this was Qian's idea.
translations.idiomatic: Former Participating Secretariat Councillor Li Lun and Director Kong Qi were extremely poor; Xiong asked that their families be supported to encourage honest officials—this was Qian's idea.

sentences.zh: 御史高胤先被逮，無行貲。

translations.literal: Censor Gao Yin had earlier been arrested and had no travel funds.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Gao Yin had earlier been arrested and had no travel funds.

sentences.zh: 謙為治裝，並恤其家。

translations.literal: Qian prepared his baggage and also supported his family.
translations.idiomatic: Qian prepared his baggage and also supported his family.

sentences.zh: 受業楊一清，聞一清將起用，貽書止之曰：「近日關中人材，連茹而起，實山川不幸。

translations.literal: He had studied under Yang Yiqing; hearing that Yiqing was about to be reappointed, he sent a letter dissuading him, saying: "Recently men of talent from Shaanxi have risen in succession like gourds on one vine—truly the misfortune of these mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied under Yang Yiqing. Hearing that Yiqing was about to be reappointed, he sent a letter dissuading him: "Recently men of talent from Shaanxi have risen in succession—truly a misfortune for the region.

sentences.zh: 獨不留三五輩為後日地耶？」

translations.literal: Will you not leave three or five men for the future?
translations.idiomatic: Will you not leave three or five men for the future?

sentences.zh: 時陜人率附瑾以進，故謙雲然。

translations.literal: At the time men of Shaanxi generally advanced by attaching themselves to Jin; therefore Qian spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: At the time men of Shaanxi generally advanced by attaching themselves to Jin; therefore Qian spoke thus.

sentences.zh: 雄下獄，謙亦被系，為怨家箠死。

translations.literal: When Xiong was cast into prison, Qian was also imprisoned and was beaten to death by an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong was imprisoned, Qian was also imprisoned and beaten to death by an enemy.

sentences.zh: 馮禎、綏德衛人。

translations.literal: Feng Zhen was a native of Guide Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zhen came from Guide Guard.

sentences.zh: 起家卒伍，累功為本衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Rising from the ranks of soldiers, through accumulated merit he became Vice Commander of his guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks through accumulated merit to vice commander of his guard.

sentences.zh: 弘治末，擢署都指揮僉事，守備偏頭關。

translations.literal: At the end of the Hongzhi reign he was promoted to acting Vice Regional Commander and garrisoned Piantou Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Hongzhi reign he was promoted to acting vice regional commander and garrisoned Piantou Pass.

sentences.zh: 尋充參將，分守寧夏西路，以勇敢聞。

translations.literal: Before long he served as Assistant Regional Commander, holding the western route of Ningxia, and was known for bravery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he served as assistant regional commander on the western route of Ningxia and was known for bravery.

sentences.zh: 寘鐇反，馳奏告變。

translations.literal: When Zhifan rebelled, he sent a rapid memorial reporting the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhifan rebelled, he sent an urgent memorial reporting the emergency.

sentences.zh: 事平，進署都指揮同知。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was advanced to acting Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled he was advanced to acting vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 已，擢副總兵，協守延綏。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Assistant Commander-in-Chief to assist in garrisoning Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to assistant commander-in-chief to assist in garrisoning Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 正德六年七月，盜起中原。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Zhengde, bandits rose in the central plain.
