translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhengde 6, bandits rose in the central plain.

sentences.zh: 詔以所部千五百人入討。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his fifteen hundred troops into the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his fifteen hundred troops into the campaign.

sentences.zh: 至阜城，遇賊。

translations.literal: Reaching Fucheng, they met the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Fucheng, they met the bandits.

sentences.zh: 禎令軍中毋顧首級、貪虜獲，遂大敗賊。

translations.literal: Zhen ordered the army not to care for heads taken or booty seized, and thus utterly defeated the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen ordered the army not to care for heads taken or booty seized, and utterly defeated the bandits.

sentences.zh: 逐北數十里，俘斬八百六十有奇。

translations.literal: Pursuing north several tens of li, they captured and beheaded more than eight hundred and sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing north for several tens of li, they captured and beheaded more than eight hundred and sixty.

sentences.zh: 進解曹州圍，執其魁朱諒。

translations.literal: Advancing, they relieved the siege of Caozhou and seized the ringleader Zhu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing, they relieved the siege of Caozhou and seized the ringleader Zhu Liang.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: In recording merit he was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was advanced to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年春，劉惠、趙鐩亂河南，連陷鹿邑、上蔡、西平、遂平、舞陽、葉，縱掠南頓、新蔡、商水、襄城，復還，駐西平。

translations.literal: The next spring, Liu Hui and Zhao San threw Henan into disorder, successively taking Luyi, Shangcai, Xiping, Suiping, Wuyang, and Ye, plundering Nandun, Xincai, Shangshui, and Xiangcheng, then returning to encamp at Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Liu Hui and Zhao San threw Henan into disorder, successively taking Luyi, Shangcai, Xiping, Suiping, Wuyang, and Ye, plundering Nandun, Xincai, Shangshui, and Xiangcheng, then returning to encamp at Xiping.

sentences.zh: 禎偕副總兵時源，參將神周、金輔擊敗之。

translations.literal: Zhen together with Assistant Commander-in-Chief Shi Yuan and Assistant Regional Commanders Shen Zhou and Jin Fu defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen together with Assistant Commander-in-Chief Shi Yuan and Assistant Regional Commanders Shen Zhou and Jin Fu defeated them.

sentences.zh: 賊奔入城，官軍塞其門。

translations.literal: The bandits fled into the city; the government army blocked the gates.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits fled into the city; government forces blocked the gates.

sentences.zh: 乘夜焚死千余人，斬首稱是，余賊潰而西。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of night they burned more than a thousand to death and took heads in corresponding number; the remaining bandits broke up and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: By night they burned more than a thousand to death and took a corresponding number of heads; the remaining bandits broke up and fled west.

sentences.zh: 巡撫鄧璋等朝崇王於汝寧，宴飲連日。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Deng Zhang and others attended upon the Prince of Chong at Runing and feasted for days on end.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Deng Zhang and others attended upon the Prince of Chong at Runing and feasted for days on end.

sentences.zh: 賊招散亡，勢復振，陷鄢陵、滎陽、汜水、鞏。

translations.literal: The bandits gathered the scattered and their power revived again; they took Yanling, Xingyang, Qishui, and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits gathered the scattered and revived; they took Yanling, Xingyang, Qishui, and Gong.

sentences.zh: 圍河南府三日，諸軍始集。

translations.literal: They besieged Henan prefecture three days before the armies assembled.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged Henan prefecture for three days before government armies assembled.

sentences.zh: 賊屯洛南，覘官軍饑疲，迎戰。

translations.literal: The bandits encamped at Luonan, observed that the government army was hungry and weary, and gave battle.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits encamped at Luonan, saw that government troops were hungry and weary, and gave battle.

sentences.zh: 右哨金輔不敢渡洛，禎及源、周方陣，而後哨參將姚信所部京軍先馳，失利，遽遁。

translations.literal: Jin Fu of the right wing dared not cross the Luo; Zhen and Yuan and Zhou were just forming ranks when Assistant Regional Commander Yao Xin of the rear wing with his capital troops charged ahead first, met defeat, and fled at once.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu of the right wing dared not cross the Luo. Zhen, Yuan, and Zhou were just forming ranks when Yao Xin of the rear wing with his capital troops charged ahead, met defeat, and fled.

sentences.zh: 陣亂，賊乘之。

translations.literal: The formation broke in disorder and the bandits seized the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: The formation broke and the bandits seized the opportunity.

sentences.zh: 禎下馬殊死鬥，援絕死焉。

translations.literal: Zhen dismounted and fought to the death; with no reinforcements he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen dismounted and fought to the death; with no reinforcements he fell.

sentences.zh: 贈洛南伯，賜祭葬，授其子大金都督僉事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Earl of Luonan, given sacrificial burial, and his son Dajin was appointed Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Earl of Luonan, granted sacrificial burial, and his son Dajin was appointed vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 後賊平，論功，復蔭一子世百戶。

translations.literal: After the bandits were pacified, in reckoning merit one more son was ennobled as hereditary hundred-household.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits were pacified, one more son was ennobled as hereditary hundred-household in reckoning merit.

sentences.zh: 明年是日，禎死所風霾大作，又明年，亦如之。

translations.literal: The next year on the same day a great wind and dust storm arose at the place of Zhen's death; the year after that, the same again.
translations.idiomatic: The next year on the same day a great wind and dust storm arose where Zhen had died; the year after, the same again.

sentences.zh: 伊王奏聞，敕有司建祠，歲以死日致祭。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi memorialized the matter; an edict ordered officials to build a shrine and perform annual sacrifice on the day of his death.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yi memorialized the matter; an edict ordered officials to build a shrine and perform annual sacrifice on the anniversary of his death.

sentences.zh: 尋用給事中李鐸言，歲給米二石，帛二疋，贍其家。

translations.literal: Before long, on the word of Supervising Secretary Li Duo, two piculs of grain and two bolts of silk were granted yearly to support his family.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on Supervising Secretary Li Duo's recommendation, two piculs of grain and two bolts of silk were granted yearly to support his family.

sentences.zh: 張俊，宣府前衛人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun was a native of the Forward Guard of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun came from the Forward Guard of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 嗣世職，為本衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary post and became regional commander of his guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the hereditary post and became commander of his guard.

sentences.zh: 累擢大同遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he was advanced to Mobile Corps General of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he was made mobile corps general of Datong.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年以功進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi, on merit, he was advanced to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 12, for merit, he was promoted to vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 火篩入大同左衛，大掠八日。

translations.literal: Huosai entered the Left Guard of Datong and plundered greatly for eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Huosai entered the Left Guard of Datong and plundered for eight days.

sentences.zh: 俊遣兵三百邀其前，復分兵三百為策應，而親禦之荊東莊。

translations.literal: Jun sent three hundred men to intercept them in front, again divided three hundred as supporting force, and personally commanded at Jingdong village.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent three hundred men to intercept them in front, divided another three hundred as a supporting force, and personally commanded at Jingdong village.

sentences.zh: 依河結營，擊卻三萬余騎。

translations.literal: Camping by the river, he struck and repelled more than thirty thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Camping by the river, he struck and repelled more than thirty thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，立擢都督僉事。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and at once promoted him to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased and at once promoted him to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 未幾，總兵官王璽失事被征，即命俊代之。

translations.literal: Before long the commander-in-chief Wang Xi lost his post through an offense and was summoned; Jun was at once ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long commander-in-chief Wang Xi was dismissed for an offense and Jun was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 其冬，以寇入戴罪，尋移鎮宣府。

translations.literal: That winter, because raiders entered he was punished by loss of merit; before long he was moved to garrison Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, because raiders entered, he was punished by loss of merit; before long he was transferred to garrison Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 中官苗逵督師延綏，檄大同、宣府卒為探騎。

translations.literal: The eunuch Miao Kui supervised the army in Yan-sui and requisitioned troops of Datong and Xuanfu as scouting cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Miao Kui supervised the army in Yan-sui and requisitioned troops of Datong and Xuanfu as scouting cavalry.

sentences.zh: 俊持不遣，逵遂劾俊。

translations.literal: Jun held back and would not release them; Kui thereupon impeached Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Jun refused to release them; Kui thereupon impeached him.

sentences.zh: 帝宥俊，而命發卒如逵言。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned Jun but ordered troops sent as Kui had said.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pardoned Jun but ordered troops sent as Kui had requested.

sentences.zh: 武宗初立，寇乘喪大入，連營二十餘里。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong first succeeded, the raiders took advantage of the mourning to enter in force, their camps stretching more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong first succeeded, raiders took advantage of the mourning to enter in force, their camps stretching more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 俊遣諸將李稽、白玉、張雄、王鎮、穆榮各帥三千人，分扼要害。

translations.literal: Jun sent the generals Li Ji, Bai Yu, Zhang Xiong, Wang Zhen, and Mu Rong, each leading three thousand men, to hold the strategic points in division.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Generals Li Ji, Bai Yu, Zhang Xiong, Wang Zhen, and Mu Rong, each with three thousand men, to hold strategic points.

sentences.zh: 俄，寇由新開口毀垣入，稽遽前迎敵；

translations.literal: Before long the raiders entered through a newly opened breach in the wall; Ji hurried forward to meet the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Before long the raiders entered through a newly opened breach in the wall. Ji hurried forward to meet them;

sentences.zh: 玉、雄、鎮、榮各帥所部拒於虞臺嶺。

translations.literal: Yu, Xiong, Zhen, and Rong each led their units to resist at Yutai Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Xiong, Zhen, and Rong each led their units to resist at Yutai Ridge.

sentences.zh: 俊急帥三千人赴援，道傷足，以兵屬都指揮曹泰。

translations.literal: Jun urgently led three thousand men to the relief; on the road he injured his foot and entrusted the troops to Regional Commander Cao Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Jun urgently led three thousand men to the relief. On the road he injured his foot and entrusted the troops to Regional Commander Cao Tai.

sentences.zh: 泰至鹿角山，被圍。

translations.literal: Tai reached Deer-Horn Mountain and was surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: Tai reached Deer-Horn Mountain and was surrounded.

sentences.zh: 俊力疾，益調兵五千人，持三日糧，馳解泰圍，復援出鎮。

translations.literal: Jun, forcing himself though ill, further mobilized five thousand men, carried three days' rations, galloped to relieve Tai's siege, and again fought his way out to rescue Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Though ill, Jun mobilized five thousand more men, carried three days' rations, galloped to relieve Tai, and fought his way out again to rescue Zhen.

sentences.zh: 又分兵救稽、玉，稽、玉亦潰圍出。

translations.literal: He again divided troops to rescue Ji and Yu; Ji and Yu also broke out of encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: He divided troops again to rescue Ji and Yu; they too broke out of encirclement.

sentences.zh: 獨雄、榮阻山澗，援絕死。

translations.literal: Only Xiong and Rong were blocked by mountain streams; with supplies cut off they died.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xiong and Rong were blocked by mountain streams; cut off from supplies, they died.

sentences.zh: 諸軍已大困，收兵還。

translations.literal: The armies were already in great distress and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The armies were already in great distress and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 寇追之，行且戰，僅得入萬全右衛城，士馬死亡無算。

translations.literal: The raiders pursued them, fighting as they went, and they barely entered the city of the Right Guard of Wanquan; soldiers and horses died beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders pursued them, fighting as they went. They barely entered Wanquan Right Guard city; soldiers and horses died beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 俊及中官劉清、巡撫李進皆征還。

translations.literal: Jun and the eunuch Liu Qing and Grand Coordinator Li Jin were all summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, the eunuch Liu Qing, and Grand Coordinator Li Jin were all summoned back.

sentences.zh: 御史郭東山言，俊扶病馳援，勸懲不宜偏廢，乃許贖罪。

translations.literal: Censor Guo Dongshan said that Jun, though ill, had galloped to the relief and that punishment should not be one-sidedly abandoned; he was therefore permitted to redeem his offense.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Guo Dongshan argued that Jun, though ill, had galloped to the relief and should not be punished one-sidedly; he was permitted to redeem his offense.

sentences.zh: 正德五年，起署都督同知，典神威營操練。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengde he was reappointed acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief to drill the Divine Might Corps.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 5 he was reappointed acting vice commissioner-in-chief to drill the Divine Might Corps.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，賊楊虎等自山西十八盤還，破武安，掠威、曲周、武城、清河、故城、景州，轉入文安，與劉六等合。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the next year the bandit Yang Hu and others returned from the Eighteen Bends of Shanxi, broke Wuan, and plundered Wei, Quzhou, Wucheng, Qinghe, Gucheng, and Jingzhou, then entered Wen'an and joined Liu Liu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the next year the bandit Yang Hu and others returned from the Eighteen Bends of Shanxi, broke Wuan, and plundered Wei, Quzhou, Wucheng, Qinghe, Gucheng, and Jingzhou, then entered Wen'an and joined Liu Liu.

sentences.zh: 都指揮桑玉屢敗，僉事許承芳請濟師。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Sang Yu was repeatedly defeated; Commissioner Xu Chengfang asked for reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Sang Yu was repeatedly defeated; Commissioner Xu Chengfang asked for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 乃命俊充副總兵，與參將王琮統京軍千人討之。

translations.literal: Jun was thereupon ordered to serve as Assistant Commander-in-Chief and, with Assistant Regional Commander Wang Cong, lead a thousand capital troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was ordered to serve as assistant commander-in-chief and, with Assistant Regional Commander Wang Cong, lead a thousand capital troops against them.

sentences.zh: 往來近畿數月，不能創賊。

translations.literal: For several months he ranged about the near capital districts and could not strike a decisive blow against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: For several months he ranged about the near capital districts without striking a decisive blow.

sentences.zh: 已，朝議調邊軍協守，賊遂連敗。

translations.literal: Before long court opinion shifted troops from the frontier to assist in defense, and the bandits suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Before long court opinion shifted frontier troops to assist in defense, and the bandits suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，劉六、劉七、齊彥名、龐文宣等敗奔登、萊海套。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year Liu Liu, Liu Qi, Qi Yanming, Pang Wenxuan, and others, defeated, fled toward the sea coasts of Deng and Lai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the next year Liu Liu, Liu Qi, Qi Yanming, Pang Wenxuan, and others, defeated, fled toward the sea coasts of Deng and Lai.

sentences.zh: 陸完檄俊軍萊州，合諸將李鋐等邀之。

translations.literal: Lu Wan requisitioned Jun's army at Laizhou to join the generals Li Hong and others in intercepting them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan requisitioned Jun's army at Laizhou to join Generals Li Hong and others in intercepting them.

sentences.zh: 賊遂北走，轉掠寶坻、香河、玉田，俊急偕許泰、郤永遏之。

translations.literal: The bandits then fled north, turning to plunder Baodi, Xianghe, and Yutian; Jun hurried with Xu Tai and Xi Yong to block them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits fled north, turning to plunder Baodi, Xianghe, and Yutian; Jun hurried with Xu Tai and Xi Yong to block them.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，勞以白金。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and rewarded them with white silver.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased and rewarded them with white silver.

sentences.zh: 賊由武清西去。

translations.literal: The bandits went off west through Wuqing.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits went off west through Wuqing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，得疾召還。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill and was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill and was recalled.

sentences.zh: 後賊平，實授都督同知。

translations.literal: After the bandits were pacified he was formally appointed Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits were pacified he was formally appointed vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he died.

sentences.zh: 俊為邊將，持廉，有謀勇。

translations.literal: Jun as a frontier general was upright and had strategy and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Jun as a frontier general was upright and possessed strategy and courage.

sentences.zh: 其歿也，家無贏資。

translations.literal: At his death his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 李鋐，大同右衛人。

translations.literal: Li Hong was a native of the Right Guard of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong came from the Right Guard of Datong.

sentences.zh: 世指揮同知，累功進都指揮僉事，充參將，協守大同。

translations.literal: Hereditary Vice Regional Commander; through accumulated merit he was advanced to Vice Regional Commander, served as Assistant Regional Commander, and assisted in garrisoning Datong.
translations.idiomatic: A hereditary vice regional commander, he rose through merit to vice regional commander, served as assistant regional commander, and assisted in garrisoning Datong.

sentences.zh: 山東盜起，詔改遊擊將軍，尋充副總兵，與俊等邀賊，復與劉暉部將傅鎧、張椿等數立功。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Shandong, an edict transferred him to Mobile Corps General; before long he was made Assistant Commander-in-Chief and, with Jun and others, intercepted the bandits; again with Liu Hui's subordinate generals Fu Kai and Zhang Chun he won merit repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Shandong, he was transferred to mobile corps general, then made assistant commander-in-chief. With Jun and others he intercepted the bandits, and with Liu Hui's subordinates Fu Kai and Zhang Chun he won repeated merit.

sentences.zh: 賊平，進都指揮同知，充總兵官，鎮鳳陽諸府。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified he was advanced to Vice Regional Commander, made commander-in-chief, and garrisoned the prefectures around Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were pacified he was promoted to vice regional commander, made commander-in-chief, and garrisoned the prefectures around Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 尋以江西盜猖獗，擢署都督僉事，與都御史俞諫同提督軍務。

translations.literal: Before long, because Jiangxi bandits were fierce, he was promoted to acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief and, together with Censor-in-Chief Yu Jian, jointly supervised military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, because Jiangxi bandits were fierce, he was promoted to acting vice commissioner-in-chief and, with Censor-in-Chief Yu Jian, jointly supervised military affairs.

sentences.zh: 賊王浩八據裴源山，憑高發矢石，官軍幾不支。

translations.literal: The bandit Wang Haoba held Peiyuan mountain, raining arrows and stones from the heights; the government army nearly could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Wang Haoba held Peiyuan mountain, raining arrows and stones from the heights, and government forces nearly gave way.

sentences.zh: 鋐下馬持刀，督將士殊死鬥，賊乃走。

translations.literal: Hong dismounted, took sword in hand, and urged the officers and soldiers to fight to the death; the bandits then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hong dismounted, sword in hand, and urged his officers and soldiers to fight to the death; the bandits then fled.

sentences.zh: 追數十里，擒之。

translations.literal: Pursuing several tens of li, they captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing them several tens of li, they captured him.

sentences.zh: 復以次討平劉昌三、胡浩三等。

translations.literal: In succession he also pacified Liu Changsan, Hu Haosan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In succession he also pacified Liu Changsan, Hu Haosan, and others.

sentences.zh: 移駐余幹，將擊遺賊之未下者，疽發背，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Moving his headquarters to Yugan, he was about to attack remnant bandits not yet subdued when a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Moving his headquarters to Yugan, he was about to attack remnant bandits when a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 詔贈右都督，蔭子都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Right Commissioner-in-Chief and ennobled his son as Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him right commissioner-in-chief and ennobled his son as vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 楊銳，字進之，蕭縣人。

translations.literal: Yang Rui, styled Jinzhi, was a native of Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rui, whose style was Jinzhi, came from Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 嗣世職，為南京羽林前衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary post and became regional commander of the Forward Guard of the Nanjing Forest of Plumes.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the hereditary post and became commander of the Forward Guard of the Nanjing Forest of Plumes.

sentences.zh: 正德初，以才擢掌龍江右衛事，督造漕舟於淮安。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde, on account of talent he was promoted to direct affairs of the Right Guard of Longjiang and supervise construction of grain-transport boats at Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengde, for talent he was promoted to direct affairs of the Right Guard of Longjiang and supervise construction of grain-transport boats at Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠有異謀，王瓊以安慶居要害，宜置戍，乃進銳署都指揮僉事，守備其地。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, harbored rebellious designs; Wang Qiong said Anqing occupied a strategic point and ought to be garrisoned; Rui was therefore advanced to acting Vice Regional Commander to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, harbored rebellious designs. Wang Qiong said Anqing occupied a strategic point and ought to be garrisoned; Rui was therefore promoted to acting vice regional commander to defend it.

sentences.zh: 銳與知府張文錦治戰艦，日督士肄水戰。

translations.literal: Rui together with Prefect Zhang Wenjin built war junks and daily drilled the men in naval combat.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and Prefect Zhang Wenjin built war junks and daily drilled the men in naval combat.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月丙子，宸濠反。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi of the sixth month of the fourteenth year, Chenhao rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day in the sixth month of the fourteenth year, Chenhao rebelled.

sentences.zh: 東下，焚彭澤、湖口、望江。

translations.literal: He went east, burning Pengze, Hukou, and Wangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He went east, burning Pengze, Hukou, and Wangjiang.

sentences.zh: 己丑，奄至安慶城下，舟五十余艘。

translations.literal: On the day jichou he suddenly reached below the walls of Anqing with more than fifty boats.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day he suddenly reached Anqing with more than fifty boats.

sentences.zh: 銳、文錦與指揮崔文、同知林有祿、通判何景昜、懷寧知縣王誥等禦之江滸。

translations.literal: Rui, Wenjin, and Regional Commander Cui Wen, Vice Prefect Lin Youlu, Transit Commissioner He Jingyang, Huaining Magistrate Wang Gao, and others defended along the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, Wenjin, Regional Commander Cui Wen, Vice Prefect Lin Youlu, Transit Commissioner He Jingyang, Huaining Magistrate Wang Gao, and others defended along the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 已，收兵入城，被圍。

translations.literal: Before long they withdrew troops into the city and were besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they withdrew into the city and were besieged.

sentences.zh: 銳、文軍城西，文錦、有祿軍城北，景抃、誥軍東南。

translations.literal: Rui and Wen defended the west of the city; Wenjin and Youlu the north; Jingyang and Gao the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and Wen defended the west; Wenjin and Youlu the north; Jingyang and Gao the southeast.

sentences.zh: 城西尤要沖，銳晝夜拒戰，殺傷賊二百余，斬其間諜，乃稍卻。

translations.literal: The west was the most critical point; Rui fought day and night, killing and wounding more than two hundred bandits and beheading their spies, and they retreated somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The west was the most critical sector. Rui fought day and night, killing and wounding more than two hundred rebels and beheading their spies, and they retreated somewhat.

sentences.zh: 七月丁酉，賊悉兵至，號十萬，舳艫相銜六十餘里。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou of the seventh month the bandits brought all their forces, claiming a hundred thousand, their boats in a line more than sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day in the seventh month the rebels brought all their forces, claiming a hundred thousand, their boats in a line more than sixty li.

sentences.zh: 宸濠乘黃艦，泊黃石磯，身自督戰。

translations.literal: Chenhao rode a yellow warship moored at Huangshi shoal and personally directed the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao rode a yellow warship moored at Huangshi shoal and personally directed the battle.

sentences.zh: 江西僉事潘鵬在賊軍，安慶人也，宸濠令諭降。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Commissioner Pan Peng was in the rebel army; he was a native of Anqing, and Chenhao ordered him to urge surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Commissioner Pan Peng was in the rebel army. A native of Anqing, Chenhao ordered him to urge surrender.

sentences.zh: 呼銳及文錦語，眾心頗搖。

translations.literal: He called to Rui and Wenjin to speak, and popular sentiment wavered somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: He called to Rui and Wenjin to speak, and morale wavered.

sentences.zh: 吏黃洲者，以大義責數之，鵬慚而退。

translations.literal: The clerk Huang Zhou, on great principle reproached him repeatedly; Peng withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk Huang Zhou reproached him on principle; Peng withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 既復持偽檄至，其家僮見，遙呼之，銳腰斬以徇。

translations.literal: When he again brought a forged edict, a household servant saw it and shouted to him from afar; Rui cut him down at the waist as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When he again brought a forged edict, a household servant saw it and shouted from afar; Rui cut him down at the waist as a warning.

sentences.zh: 將射鵬，鵬遁去，眾心乃定。

translations.literal: He was about to shoot Peng; Peng fled, and popular sentiment was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to shoot Peng; Peng fled, and morale was settled.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，圍城數周，攻益急。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger encircled the city several rounds and pressed the assault ever harder.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in anger encircled the city several times and pressed the assault harder.

sentences.zh: 銳等殊死戰。

translations.literal: Rui and the others fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and the others fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 賊雲樓數十瞰城中，城中亦造飛樓射賊，夜縋人焚賊樓。

translations.literal: The bandits raised cloud-ladders several tens in number overlooking the city; the city also built flying towers to shoot at the bandits, and at night men were lowered to burn the bandit towers.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels raised dozens of cloud-ladders overlooking the city; the defenders built flying towers to shoot back, and at night lowered men to burn the rebel towers.

sentences.zh: 賊置天梯，廣二丈，高於城，版蔽之，前後有門，伏兵其中，輪轉以薄城。

translations.literal: The bandits set up scaling ladders two zhang wide, higher than the walls, covered with boards, with doors before and behind and hidden soldiers within, wheeled to press against the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels set up scaling ladders two zhang wide, higher than the walls, boarded over with doors front and back and hidden soldiers within, wheeled to press the walls.

sentences.zh: 城上束葦沃膏，燃其端，梯稍近即投之，須臾盡焚，賊多死。

translations.literal: On the wall they bound reeds and poured grease, lit the ends, and when a ladder drew near cast them down; in an instant all were burned and many bandits died.
translations.idiomatic: Defenders bound reeds, poured grease, lit them, and when a ladder drew near cast them down; in an instant all were burned and many rebels died.

sentences.zh: 時軍衛卒不滿百，乘城皆民兵。

translations.literal: At the time garrison soldiers numbered less than a hundred; those defending the walls were all local militia.
translations.idiomatic: At the time garrison soldiers numbered less than a hundred; those on the walls were all local militia.

sentences.zh: 老弱婦女饋餉，人運石一二，數日積如山。

translations.literal: The old, weak, women, and children supplied food; each person carried one or two stones, and in several days they piled like a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The old, weak, women, and children supplied food; each person carried one or two stones, and in days they piled like a mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊攻城，城上或投石，或沸湯沃之，賊輒傷。

translations.literal: When the bandits attacked, the defenders cast stones or poured boiling liquid; the bandits were always wounded.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels attacked, defenders cast stones or poured boiling liquid; the rebels were always wounded.

sentences.zh: 銳等射書賊營，諭令解散，有亡去者。

translations.literal: Rui and the others shot letters into the rebel camp urging them to disperse, and some fled.
translations.idiomatic: Rui shot letters into the rebel camp urging dispersal, and some fled.

sentences.zh: 乃募死士夜劫賊營，賊大驚擾，比曉稍定。

translations.literal: They then recruited dare-to-die men to raid the rebel camp by night; the bandits were greatly alarmed and disturbed, and by dawn were somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: They recruited dare-to-die men to raid the rebel camp by night; the rebels were greatly alarmed, and by dawn somewhat calmed.

sentences.zh: 宸濠慚憤，謂其下曰：「安慶且不克，安望南都。」

translations.literal: Chenhao, shamed and enraged, said to his followers: "If we cannot take Anqing, what hope have we for the Southern Capital?
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao, shamed and enraged, said to his followers, "If we cannot take Anqing, what hope have we for the Southern Capital?

sentences.zh: 會聞伍文定等破南昌，遂解圍去。

translations.literal: It happened that word came that Wu Wending and others had broken Nanchang, and he thereupon lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that Wu Wending and others had broken Nanchang, and he lifted the siege and departed.

sentences.zh: 文出城襲擊，又破之，旬有八日而圍解。

translations.literal: Wenjin sallied from the city to strike and again defeated them; in all eighteen days and the siege was raised.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin sallied from the city to strike and defeated them again; after eighteen days the siege was raised.

sentences.zh: 事聞，武宗大喜，擢銳參將，分守安徽池、太、寧國及九江、鐃、黃。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Emperor Wuzong was greatly pleased, promoted Rui to Assistant Regional Commander, and divided his command over Chizhou, Taiping, Ningguo in Anhui and Jiujiang, Rao, and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, Emperor Wuzong was greatly pleased, promoted Rui to assistant regional commander, and divided his command over Chizhou, Taiping, Ningguo in Anhui and Jiujiang, Rao, and Huang.

sentences.zh: 銳薦鄭嶽、胡世寧，帝即召用。

translations.literal: Rui recommended Zheng Yue and Hu Shining; the Emperor at once summoned and employed them.
translations.idiomatic: Rui recommended Zheng Yue and Hu Shining; the Emperor at once summoned and employed them.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，論功，擢都督僉事，蔭子世千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, in reckoning merit he was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief and his son was ennobled as hereditary thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, for merit he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief and his son ennobled as hereditary thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 再遷僉書左府，改南京右府。

translations.literal: Again he was transferred to Secretary of the Left Military Commission and then to the Right Commission of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to secretary of the Left Military Commission and then to the Right Commission of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 充總兵官，鎮遼東。

translations.literal: He served as commander-in-chief garrisoning Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commander-in-chief garrisoning Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 改督漕運，鎮淮安。

translations.literal: He was changed to supervise grain transport and garrison Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to supervise grain transport and garrison Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年為巡按御史李循義劾罷，逾年卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiajing he was impeached and dismissed by Touring Censor Li Xunyi; he died the year after.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 10 he was impeached and dismissed by Touring Censor Li Xunyi; he died the following year.

sentences.zh: 崔文，世為安慶衛指揮使，守城勞亞於銳。

translations.literal: Cui Wen, for generations regional commander of Anqing Guard, in labor defending the city was second only to Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wen, for generations commander of Anqing Guard, in defending the city was second only to Rui.

sentences.zh: 世宗錄其功，超三階為都指揮使，蔭子世百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong recorded his merit, advanced him three ranks to Regional Commander, and ennobled his son as hereditary hundred-household.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong recorded his merit, advanced him three ranks to regional commander, and ennobled his son as hereditary hundred-household.

sentences.zh: 江、淮多盜，廷議設總兵官，督上下江防，擢文都督僉事任之。

translations.literal: Bandits were numerous on the Yangzi and Huai; court opinion set up a commander-in-chief to supervise upper and lower river defense; Wen was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief for the post.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were numerous on the Yangzi and Huai; the court set up a commander-in-chief for upper and lower river defense; Wen was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 改蒞南京前府，專督操江、久之，卒。

translations.literal: He was changed to direct the Forward Commission of Nanjing and specialized in supervising Yangzi defense; after a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to direct the Forward Commission of Nanjing and specialized in Yangzi defense; after a long while he died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：衛青等當承平時，不逞竊發，列城擾攘，賴其戡定。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When Wei Qing and the others lived in an age of peace, restless elements would steal forth and disturb the cities; it was by them that order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: In an age of peace, when restless elements stole forth and disturbed the cities, it was men such as Wei Qing who restored order.

sentences.zh: 雖所敵非堅，然勇敢力戰，功多可紀。

translations.literal: Though their foes were not formidable, they fought bravely and their achievements are largely worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Though their foes were not formidable, they fought bravely and their achievements are largely worth recording.

sentences.zh: 或遂身膏原野，若何洪、劉雄、馮禎輩，壯節有足惜者。

translations.literal: Some even gave their bodies to the wild plain, such as He Hong, Liu Xiong, Feng Zhen, and their kind—stalwart conduct well worth mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Some even gave their bodies on the battlefield, such as He Hong, Liu Xiong, and Feng Zhen—stalwart conduct well worth mourning.

sentences.zh: 鉞以心計定亂，銳以城守摧逆，幹城之寄，克稱廟謨。

translations.literal: Yue by stratagem settled disorder; Rui by defending the city crushed rebellion—the charge of shielding the state well fulfilled the court's design.
translations.idiomatic: Yue settled the rebellion through stratagem; Rui crushed it by holding the city. In the charge of shielding the realm, both lived up to the court's design.

sentences.zh: 神英、曹雄亦有勞績，而以附閹損名，且獲罪。

translations.literal: Shen Ying and Cao Xiong also had labor and achievement, yet by attaching themselves to eunuchs they damaged their names and moreover incurred guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ying and Cao Xiong also won merit in the field, yet by attaching themselves to eunuchs they ruined their reputations and incurred guilt besides.

sentences.zh: 為將者其以跅弛為戒哉。

translations.literal: Let commanders take lax discipline as their warning!
translations.idiomatic: Let every commander take lax discipline as a warning!
